reader.requirement: Data stored into a numeric edited receiver is aligned by decimal point with zero fill or truncation at either end within the receiver's character positions, except where editing (Z, *, floating $ + -, BLANK WHEN ZERO) replaces leading zeros, for every 1985 editing symbol including P, B, 0, CR/DB and a leading period.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel < 2002: a digit-only ALL literal into a numeric-edited receiver is repeated to the picture's full length and taken as an integer (85) instead of the receiver's digit positions at its scale (2002+)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior in MoveEmitter.cs, NumericRenderer.cs, CobolEdit.cs: only AllLiteralNumber consults the edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: MOVE ALL "12" TO PIC ZZ9.99 edits the integer 121212 as 212.00 at 85; every other edited alignment is the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f04_01 covers 999.99, ZZ9.99, Z9.9 and ZZZ from literals; not exercised are CR, floating $, check protection, +, B insertion, P in an edited picture, BLANK WHEN ZERO, a leading period, signed and alphanumeric senders and ALL literals

probes.expected: -123.456 aligned and truncated into ZZ9.99CR, $$$9.9, ***9.99- and +ZZ; 1234.5 into 99B99 is 12 34; 1234567 into ZZ9PP keeps 345; zero and 0.004 into ZZ.ZZ BLANK WHEN ZERO blank; 12.3456 into 9.999 is 2.345; ALL "12" at 85 is 212.00; "12345" into ZZ9.99 is 345.00; 12.345 into .99 is .34; 0.9 into ZZZZ is blank

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.6 GR2  (4.3.6 Standard Alignment Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: ConvertSource's numeric-edited arm transfers the value to the mask's receiver scale (truncating the fraction) and CobolEdit.Format places the digits, dropping high-order digits and zero-filling or replacing leading zeros per the mask. All fourteen probe lines match the rule.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-187/ra1.cob (runs/ra1-001, --std 85): edited sender into edited receiver -$1,234.50 -> ZZ9.99CR '234.50CR'; 12345 into $$$9 '$345' (floating digit positions truncate left); 1.5 into **,**9.99 '*****1.50'; 0.0012345 into PP99+ '12+' (P to the left of the digits); 123456 into ++++9 '+3456'; 12345 into 9909 '3405'; -12345.678 into Z,ZZ9.99DB '2,345.67DB'; COMP 7 into ZZ9.99 '  7.00'. All aligned by the point with truncation at both ends. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.6 GR2  (4.3.6 Standard Alignment Rules)  the text is in GR2'.
